profile.description: Bridge to your Hermes Agent so you can talk, collaborate, and delegate — including coaching Hermes install and API setup when needed.

memory.content: Prefer hermes peer for Hermes talk/delegate; never print API_SERVER_KEY or HERMES_PEER_* keys; never put Bearer tokens on the command line.
Hermes API (often port 8642) is not the Grok Bot box gateway (1340).
On first chat or when hermes peer list is empty / peer calls fail, run the Hermes bridge setup skill before other Hermes skills.
After setup, use shared skills: hermes-conversation, hermes-collaborate, hermes-delegate-collect, hermes-delegate-own, hermes-delegate-pair.

skills.name: Hermes bridge setup
skills.description: Use when connecting a Grok Bot to Hermes for the first time (or repairing the bridge): detect install, coach install-from-zero if needed, enable the API server, register hermes peer, and smoke-test.
skills.content:
---
name: Hermes bridge setup
description: >-
  Use when connecting a Grok Bot to Hermes for the first time (or repairing the
  bridge): detect install, coach install-from-zero if needed, enable the API
  server, register hermes peer, and smoke-test.
---
# Hermes bridge setup

First-run (and repair) playbook so a **Grok Bot** can reach a **Hermes Agent** API via `hermes peer`. This skill **writes instructions and runs checks** — it does not assume Hermes is missing. If Hermes is already installed and healthy, skip straight to peer + smoke.

This is for **adopters** of a Hermes Bridge-style bot. Do not bake in one lab's host IP, roster, or keys.

## When to use

- First chat with a Hermes Bridge bot (or any Grok Bot that needs Hermes)
- `hermes peer list` is empty / peer calls fail
- User asks to connect, install, or repair Hermes for bridging

Don't use for:

- Normal talk/collab/delegate once a peer works → [Hermes conversation](sand-workflow:hermes-conversation) and siblings
- Messaging other Grok Bots via box gateway `:1340` (different product)

## Hard rules

- Never print `API_SERVER_KEY`, `HERMES_PEER_*_KEY`, or any Bearer token
- Never put secrets on the shell command line in a way that lands in chat logs; prefer `hermes peer add` with key supplied in a way that stays out of the transcript (env file / secure prompt). If you must pass `--key`, do not echo the command back to the user with the key visible
- Never Funnel or publicly expose the Hermes API
- Hermes API (often port `8642`) ≠ Grok Bot box gateway (`1340`)

## Official docs (point users here)

- Quickstart: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart
- Installation: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation
- API server: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/api-server
- Env vars: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/environment-variables

## Ladder

Run in order. Stop when the current step's completion check passes.

### 1. Detect

```text
which hermes
hermes --version
hermes peer list
```

Optional health (no auth):

```text
curl -sS "$HERMES_API_BASE/health"
```

Use `HERMES_API_BASE` like `http://127.0.0.1:8642` or the user's tailnet/LAN URL — **ask them**; do not invent a host.

| Result | Action |
|---|---|
| No `hermes` on PATH | Go to step 2 (install-from-zero) |
| `hermes` present, API health fails | Go to step 3 (enable API) |
| API healthy, no peer / peer errors | Go to step 4 (register peer) |
| Peer listed with key set | Go to step 5 (smoke) |

### 2. Install-from-zero (only if needed)

Coach the user through the official quickstart/installation pages. Typical shape:

1. Install Hermes Agent per their OS (official install doc)
2. Ensure `hermes` is on PATH for the same environment this Grok Bot's shell uses
3. Run provider setup (`hermes setup` / portal as docs prescribe) — **user** completes browser/device login and 2FA
4. Verify: `hermes --version` and a trivial local check from the docs (e.g. status/doctor if available)

Completion: `which hermes` succeeds. Then continue to step 3.

Do **not** paste full installer scripts into chat as a substitute for the official docs; link and verify.

### 3. Enable API server

In the Hermes home `.env` (usually `~/.hermes/.env` or `$HERMES_HOME/.env`):

```bash
API_SERVER_ENABLED=true
API_SERVER_HOST=127.0.0.1
API_SERVER_PORT=8642
API_SERVER_KEY=<user-chosen-secret>
```

Notes:

- Bind `127.0.0.1` for same-machine; use a tailnet/LAN address only if the Grok Bot shell is on another host
- Generate a strong key; store only in `.env`; never repeat it in chat
- Start/restart the gateway so the API platform is up (`hermes gateway` / `hermes gateway run` per their install)

Completion: `GET $HERMES_API_BASE/health` returns JSON with ok/status for hermes-agent. `GET $HERMES_API_BASE/v1/models` without a key should be **401** (proves auth is on).

### 4. Register peer

Pick a short peer name (example: `local` or `hermes`).

```text
hermes peer add <name> --url <HERMES_API_BASE> --key <API_SERVER_KEY>
hermes peer list
```

Completion: `hermes peer list` shows `<name>` with key set. Remember the name as the default peer for later skills (write a portable memory: "default Hermes peer is <name>").

### 5. Smoke

```text
hermes peer dm <name> "Reply exactly: bridge-pong ok"
```

Completion: printed reply contains `bridge-pong ok`, exit code 0.

### 6. Hand off

Tell the user they're connected. Offer:

- [Hermes conversation](sand-workflow:hermes-conversation) — sync chat
- [Hermes collaborate](sand-workflow:hermes-collaborate) — multi-turn
- [Hermes delegate collect](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-collect) — fire-and-collect
- [Hermes delegate own](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-own) — Hermes owns the workstream
- [Hermes delegate pair](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-pair) — pair until accept

## Failure table

| Symptom | Likely fix |
|---|---|
| `hermes: command not found` | Install + PATH (step 2) |
| Connection refused on API port | Gateway not running or wrong `HERMES_API_BASE` (step 3) |
| HTTP 401 on peer/API calls | Key mismatch — re-run `hermes peer add` with current `API_SERVER_KEY` |
| Peer dm hangs a long time | Hermes is working a tool-heavy turn — wait; for long jobs use delegate collect/own |
| Works on host terminal but not from Grok Bot shell | Different PATH / different machine — install CLI where the bot's shell runs, or point peer URL at the reachable Hermes host |

## Verification

- Detect → (optional install) → API health → peer list → `bridge-pong ok`
- No secrets appear in the user-visible transcript
- Default peer name saved for the bot's later skills

skills.name: Hermes conversation
skills.description: Use when a Grok Bot needs a short sync conversation with Hermes Agent (ask, ping, clarify, get a reply in one turn).
skills.content:
---
name: Hermes conversation
description: >-
  Use when a Grok Bot needs a short sync conversation with Hermes Agent (ask,
  ping, clarify, get a reply in one turn).
---
# Hermes conversation

Talk to a **local or remote Hermes Agent** over its **API server** using `hermes peer dm`. This is sync chat: you send one message, Hermes runs a turn, you get the reply printed.

Do **not** use the Grok Bot box gateway (`:1340`) for this — that is a different product (messaging Grok Bots). Hermes lives on its own API (typically `:8642`).

## When to use

- Ask Hermes a question and need the answer now
- Ping / health-style check that Hermes is responsive as an agent
- One-shot clarify before a larger handoff

Don't use for:

- Long jobs you will poll later → [Hermes delegate collect](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-collect)
- Work Hermes should own while you move on → [Hermes delegate own](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-own)
- Multi-turn pairing until a goal is done → [Hermes collaborate](sand-workflow:hermes-collaborate) or [Hermes delegate pair](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-pair)
- Messaging other Grok Bots → grok-bot-gateway / box `:1340`
- Peer missing / Hermes not connected → [Hermes bridge setup](sand-workflow:hermes-bridge-setup)

## Prerequisites

- `hermes` CLI on PATH
- Peer registered: `hermes peer list` shows a name with `[key set]`
- If missing: run [Hermes bridge setup](sand-workflow:hermes-bridge-setup) (or `hermes peer add <name> --url <HERMES_API_BASE> --key <API_SERVER_KEY>` — never print the key)
- Auth stays in `~/.hermes/.env` as `HERMES_PEER_<NAME>_KEY` — never echo, never put in chat
- Default peer: memory "default Hermes peer is …" if set, else the name from `hermes peer list`

## How to run

```text
hermes peer list
hermes peer dm <peer> "<message>"
```

Optional agent/profile on a multiplexed peer: `hermes peer dm <peer>/<agent> "..."`.

## Procedure

1. Resolve peer with memory or `hermes peer list`. Example names include `local` or `hermes` — use whatever is registered.
2. Put your Grok Bot identity in the message text (Hermes does not know who you are otherwise), e.g. `Message from Grok Bot <name>: ...`
3. Keep the ask self-contained; one `dm` is one Hermes turn.
4. Completion: CLI prints Hermes's reply (exit 0). Cite that reply to the user; do not invent it.
5. Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` delivery/peer error, `2` usage error.

## Pitfalls

- Do not `curl` with `Authorization: Bearer` on the command line (shell history). Prefer `hermes peer`.
- Do not Funnel the Hermes API; keep it local or private network.
- `hermes peer` targets **Hermes gateways**, not Grok Bot `:1340`.
- A successful HTTP health check is not a conversation — use `dm` for agent replies.

## Verification

- `hermes peer dm <peer> 'Reply exactly: hermes-pong ok'` returns that line.
- No API keys appear in the transcript or logs you produce.

skills.name: Hermes collaborate
skills.description: Use when a Grok Bot and Hermes must work together over several turns toward a shared goal (plan, review, iterate) without treating Hermes as a fire-and-forget worker.
skills.content:
---
name: Hermes collaborate
description: >-
  Use when a Grok Bot and Hermes must work together over several turns toward a
  shared goal (plan, review, iterate) without treating Hermes as a
  fire-and-forget worker.
---
# Hermes collaborate

Multi-turn collaboration with Hermes over `hermes peer dm` (or session-sticky HTTP if you already hold a session id). You keep the driver's seat: propose, Hermes responds, you steer, repeat until the shared goal is met or the user says stop.

## When to use

- Joint planning, review, or design with Hermes
- Iterating on an artifact Hermes can produce (draft, analysis, script) with your feedback each turn
- You need Hermes's capabilities but will stay in the loop

Don't use for:

- Single Q&A → [Hermes conversation](sand-workflow:hermes-conversation)
- Hand off and only collect a final result → [Hermes delegate collect](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-collect)
- Hermes should own the workstream with occasional check-ins → [Hermes delegate own](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-own)
- Peer missing → [Hermes bridge setup](sand-workflow:hermes-bridge-setup)

## Prerequisites

Same as conversation: `hermes` CLI, registered peer with key set, never print keys. See [Hermes conversation](sand-workflow:hermes-conversation). Resolve `<peer>` from memory or `hermes peer list`.

## How to run

```text
hermes peer dm <peer> "<turn 1: goal + constraints + who you are>"
hermes peer dm <peer> "<turn 2: feedback / next ask>"
# repeat until done
```

For stronger continuity, prefer HTTP session chat (same `session_id`) when you already load auth from env in-process — still never print the key:

```text
POST /api/sessions  →  POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat  (repeat)  →  GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages
```

API base is typically `http://127.0.0.1:8642` or the user's private-network Hermes URL — do not hard-code a lab host.

## Procedure

1. Open with a clear shared goal, constraints (non-destructive / non-spend unless the user said otherwise), success criteria, and your bot name.
2. Each turn: one concrete ask; quote what you accepted from Hermes's last reply.
3. Prefer small steps Hermes can finish in one turn.
4. After each reply, decide: continue, pivot, or stop and report to the user.
5. Completion: goal met (or explicit stop) with a short trail of what Hermes said (cited), not a vibe summary.
6. If a turn needs a long job, switch that slice to [Hermes delegate collect](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-collect) then resume collaboration with the result.

## Pitfalls

- Don't dump a giant brief then go silent — that is own-workstream, not collaborate.
- Don't start parallel `dm` storms; one conversational thread at a time unless the user asked for fan-out.
- Identify yourself every few turns if the session might be ambiguous.
- Approvals / spend / destructive ops stay with the user — do not ask Hermes to bypass that.

## Verification

- At least two successful `dm` (or session chat) turns on the same goal.
- Final report to the user includes Hermes quotes and the decision you made.

skills.name: Hermes delegate collect
skills.description: Use when a Grok Bot should hand Hermes a bounded task, get a run id, poll to completion, and return Hermes's final output (fire-and-collect).
skills.content:
---
name: Hermes delegate collect
description: >-
  Use when a Grok Bot should hand Hermes a bounded task, get a run id, poll to
  completion, and return Hermes's final output (fire-and-collect).
---
# Hermes delegate — fire and collect

Hand Hermes a task, get a `run_id`, poll until done, bring the **final output** back into the Grok Bot chat. Default async delegation mode.

## When to use

- One bounded job Hermes can finish without mid-flight pairing
- You need a result ticket (`run_id`) and a clear completed output
- Parallel-friendly: you can start the run then do other work while polling

Don't use for:

- Short sync Q&A → [Hermes conversation](sand-workflow:hermes-conversation)
- You will steer every turn → [Hermes collaborate](sand-workflow:hermes-collaborate) or [Hermes delegate pair](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-pair)
- Hermes should keep owning a long workstream with light check-ins → [Hermes delegate own](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-own)
- Peer missing → [Hermes bridge setup](sand-workflow:hermes-bridge-setup)

## Prerequisites

- `hermes` CLI; peer registered (`hermes peer list`) or remembered default peer
- Never print `API_SERVER_KEY` / `HERMES_PEER_*_KEY`
- Prefer non-destructive / non-spend tasks unless the user explicitly authorized otherwise

## How to run

```text
# from a file (good for longer prompts)
hermes peer run <peer> --idempotency-key <stable-ticket-id> < task.txt

# then poll
hermes peer status <peer> <run_id>

# if you must abort
hermes peer stop <peer> <run_id>
```

HTTP equivalent (auth from env in-process, never on argv):

```text
POST /v1/runs   (+ Idempotency-Key)
GET  /v1/runs/{run_id}
GET  /v1/runs/{run_id}/events   # optional SSE
POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/stop
```

## Procedure

1. Write a self-contained task: goal, constraints, success criteria, your bot identity, "reply with the deliverable when done."
2. Choose a stable `--idempotency-key` (same key retries safely; don't reuse for a different job).
3. `hermes peer run <peer> ...` → record `run_id` (and session_id if printed).
4. Poll `hermes peer status` until `completed` / failed / stopped. Back off (e.g. 2s+); don't hammer.
5. Completion: status `completed` and an `output` (or explicit failure). Deliver that output to the user; cite `run_id`.
6. Do not start a duplicate run for the same ticket while one is `running`.

## Pitfalls

- `started` / HTTP 202 is **not** done — always poll to a terminal status.
- Idempotency keys are durable (~24h on this API) — colliding keys replay the old run.
- Don't confuse Hermes `:8642` with Grok Bot `:1340`.

## Verification

- A smoke run with input "Reply exactly: run-pong ok" reaches `completed` with that output.
- No secrets in chat.

skills.name: Hermes delegate own
skills.description: Use when Hermes should own a longer workstream: start an async run, check in or unblock occasionally, and avoid turn-by-turn pairing.
skills.content:
---
name: Hermes delegate own
description: >-
  Use when Hermes should own a longer workstream: start an async run, check in
  or unblock occasionally, and avoid turn-by-turn pairing.
---
# Hermes delegate — own workstream

Hermes **owns** the workstream. You start an async run (or a clear ownership brief), then only **check in / unblock / steer lightly**. You do not pair every turn. Report progress to the user; don't micromanage Hermes.

## When to use

- Multi-step or longer missions Hermes should drive
- You need to stay available for other work while Hermes continues
- Occasional steer or stop is enough; full pair loop is overkill

Don't use for:

- Need the answer in one sync turn → [Hermes conversation](sand-workflow:hermes-conversation)
- Tight back-and-forth until done → [Hermes delegate pair](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-pair) or [Hermes collaborate](sand-workflow:hermes-collaborate)
- Single bounded job with immediate collect → [Hermes delegate collect](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-collect)
- Peer missing → [Hermes bridge setup](sand-workflow:hermes-bridge-setup)

## Prerequisites

Same peer/auth rules as other Hermes skills. Prefer `hermes peer run` so you have a `run_id` to status/steer/stop. Resolve `<peer>` from memory or `hermes peer list`.

## How to run

```text
hermes peer run <peer> --idempotency-key <mission-id> < mission.txt
hermes peer status <peer> <run_id>          # check-in
# HTTP steer when needed:
# POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/steer   {"message":"<guidance>"}
hermes peer stop <peer> <run_id>            # abort if the user says stop
```

## Procedure

1. Write a **mission brief**: goal, constraints, definition of done, reporting expectations, your bot identity, what Hermes may decide alone vs must escalate to the user.
2. Start with `hermes peer run` + stable mission idempotency key. Save `run_id`.
3. Tell the user the mission is with Hermes and give the `run_id`.
4. Check in with `status` at coarse intervals (or when the user asks). If blocked on approval/spend/secrets, surface that to the user — don't invent approvals.
5. Steer only when direction changes; prefer one steer message with clear guidance.
6. Completion: terminal status + output, or the user cancels (`stop`). Summarize outcome with `run_id` and cited output.

## Ownership rules

- Hermes decides sequencing and tools inside the brief.
- You own user communication and any Grok Bot–side side effects.
- Destructive / spend / identity actions still need the user.

## Pitfalls

- Don't convert this into a hidden pair loop (constant steers).
- Don't start a second mission run for the same key while one is live.
- A quiet `running` status is normal for long jobs — check events if you need detail (`GET /v1/runs/{id}/events`).

## Verification

- Mission starts with a `run_id`; a later `status` shows progress or `completed` with output.
- The user was told who owns the work (Hermes) and how to stop it.

skills.name: Hermes delegate pair
skills.description: Use when a Grok Bot delegates a goal to Hermes but must pair turn-by-turn (review, redirect, accept) until acceptance criteria pass.
skills.content:
---
name: Hermes delegate pair
description: >-
  Use when a Grok Bot delegates a goal to Hermes but must pair turn-by-turn
  (review, redirect, accept) until acceptance criteria pass.
---
# Hermes delegate — pair

Delegate a goal but **pair until done**: alternate Hermes work and your feedback in a tight loop. Use when the task is too interactive for fire-and-collect, but you still frame it as delegated work (Hermes executes; you accept/reject/redirect).

## When to use

- Implementation or writing that needs review each slice
- Ambiguous goals that need rapid clarification mid-flight
- You want Hermes to do the heavy lifting, but quality gates stay with you

Don't use for:

- One-shot Q&A → [Hermes conversation](sand-workflow:hermes-conversation)
- Open-ended joint brainstorming without a delegated outcome → [Hermes collaborate](sand-workflow:hermes-collaborate)
- Truly async "ping me when done" → [Hermes delegate collect](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-collect)
- Hermes should drive for a long time alone → [Hermes delegate own](sand-workflow:hermes-delegate-own)
- Peer missing → [Hermes bridge setup](sand-workflow:hermes-bridge-setup)

## Prerequisites

Peer + `hermes` CLI; never print keys. Resolve `<peer>` from memory or `hermes peer list`. Session continuity helps: prefer repeated `hermes peer dm` with explicit "continuing our pairing on <goal>" or HTTP `/api/sessions/{id}/chat` with a saved session id.

## How to run

```text
hermes peer dm <peer> "<delegate brief: goal, constraints, first slice>"
hermes peer dm <peer> "<accept / redirect / next slice>"
# loop until acceptance criteria met
```

For a slice that is itself long, nest collect:

```text
hermes peer run <peer> --idempotency-key <slice-id> < slice.txt
hermes peer status <peer> <run_id>
# then dm with the collected output + your verdict
```

## Procedure

1. Open with: delegated goal, constraints, **acceptance criteria**, first slice only, your bot identity.
2. Hermes returns a slice → you verify (run tests, read output, check claims).
3. Reply with accept / changes requested / stop. Be specific; paste evidence.
4. Repeat until acceptance criteria pass or the user stops the pairing.
5. Completion: final accepted artifact + short decision log (what changed each round). Cite Hermes lines that matter.

## Pairing contract (put in the first message)

- Hermes proposes or produces; you decide accept/reject.
- One slice per turn unless you explicitly batch.
- No spend / destructive / secret exfil without the user.
- If stuck twice on the same blocker, escalate to the user instead of looping forever.

## Pitfalls

- Unlimited pairing without acceptance criteria wastes both agents — write the done-check first.
- Don't run parallel pair threads on the same goal.
- Don't pretend fire-and-collect output is "paired" if you never reviewed it.

## Verification

- ≥2 round-trips with an explicit accept or change-request each time.
- Final user update states the acceptance criteria and whether they passed.
